title: The Great Gildersleeve
paragraphs: A pioneering situation comedy following the pompous but good-hearted Throckmorton P. Gildersleeve as he raises his niece and nephew and becomes part of everyday life in the town of Summerfield.

NBC family/situation comedy spun off from Fibber McGee and Molly. GRH includes a May 1941 audition, the regular series, several partially dated AFRS/AFRTS items, and one April 1957 archive item after the documented NBC finale.

GRH documents the program through Harold Peary weekly era (August 31, 1941 to June 14, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Willard Waterman weekly era (September 6, 1950 to June 2, 1954) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], 15-minute strip era (September 26, 1954 to June 23, 1955) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Final weekly era (October 6, 1955 to March 21, 1957) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Walter Tetley (performer on 473 recordings), Lillian Randolph (performer on 462 recordings), Richard LeGrand (performer on 417 recordings), Earle Ross (performer on 363 recordings), [[person|hal-peary|Hal Peary]] (performer on 311 recordings), Jack Meakin (music on 260 recordings, composer on 41 recordings, and performer on 33 recordings), and Andy White (writer on 241 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Youth, school, and parenting, Small-town civic life, Romance and courtship, Family and household life, Holiday episodes, and Money and household economics.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Radio spin-off and family-sitcom development and Network radio comedy during the television transition.
